account: Vyntra's “Fraud Cases” page was published 4 April 2022 per its page metadata; the cases themselves are undated. It states that “Our solutions stop the fraud before the money leaves the bank” and lists about two dozen short case studies at unnamed banks. One is an account takeover after pharming stopped before a CHF 19,990 payment. Another is an impersonation that led a bank employee to validate a CHF 1,000,000 transaction, blocked because the beneficiary was unusual at bank level. There are vishing, tech-support, CEO-fraud, business-email-compromise, romance and invoice-redirection cases. Their payments of EUR 22,114, EUR 33,170, USD 7,500, GBP 21,000, EUR 125,000, EUR 170,000, USD 100,000, USD 170,000 and USD 850,000 were stopped. Transaction or e-banking session variables (beneficiary, country, amount, currency, browser, screen resolution, language) did not match the customer's or bank's usual profile. There are two internal-fraud cases. In one case “fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) from the second bank's ATMs”. The models had flagged unusual timing and frequency of withdrawals. One entry still names “NetGuardians solution”, the Swiss company that merged with Belgium's Intix to form Vyntra in June 2025 (FinTech Global, 19 June 2025). No customer or bank is identified, and no dated event, regulator finding or court record is supplied. The current page labels the CHF 19,990 example as Switzerland. The page is the vendor's own account.

ai_role.statement: The evidence is limited to the maker's account. Vyntra's page attributes each block to its AI risk models detecting variables outside the customer's or bank's usual profile. No customer, bank, date or official record is available to assess whether the models, rather than staff or other controls, produced the outcome. The AI's contribution is not established.

fields.account: Vyntra's “Fraud Cases” page was published 4 April 2022 per its page metadata; the cases themselves are undated. It states that “Our solutions stop the fraud before the money leaves the bank” and lists about two dozen short case studies at unnamed banks. One is an account takeover after pharming stopped before a CHF 19,990 payment. Another is an impersonation that led a bank employee to validate a CHF 1,000,000 transaction, blocked because the beneficiary was unusual at bank level. There are vishing, tech-support, CEO-fraud, business-email-compromise, romance and invoice-redirection cases. Their payments of EUR 22,114, EUR 33,170, USD 7,500, GBP 21,000, EUR 125,000, EUR 170,000, USD 100,000, USD 170,000 and USD 850,000 were stopped. Transaction or e-banking session variables (beneficiary, country, amount, currency, browser, screen resolution, language) did not match the customer's or bank's usual profile. There are two internal-fraud cases. In one case “fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) from the second bank's ATMs”. The models had flagged unusual timing and frequency of withdrawals. One entry still names “NetGuardians solution”, the Swiss company that merged with Belgium's Intix to form Vyntra in June 2025 (FinTech Global, 19 June 2025). No customer or bank is identified, and no dated event, regulator finding or court record is supplied. The current page labels the CHF 19,990 example as Switzerland. The page is the vendor's own account.
